target: bract PO:0009055 part of peduncle PO:0009053, absent PATO:0000462. The involucral bracts PO:0009045 (phyllaries) are present, with squarrose tips
fix: In Asteraceae, 'ebracteate' on a peduncle or head stalk means the stalk has no bracts. It never means the involucral bracts (phyllaries) are absent. Keep the stalk as the absence's scope; never record it as a taxon-wide 'bract absent'.
reason: The phyllaries are described (squarrose tips), so only the stalk is without bracts.

target: corolla PO:0009059 of the pistillate (ray) flowers PO:0025331: no lamina (ligule/limb). The leaf lamina PO:0020039 is present (minutely glandular)
fix: In Asteraceae, 'lacking laminae' in a floret statement means the corollas of the ray or pistillate florets have no ligule or limb. It must never become 'leaf lamina absent'. Map 'lamina' to the leaf only when the statement is about leaves.
reason: Erigeron calvus is the 'bald' fleabane: its pistillate florets have no rays. Its leaves have blades.

target: caudex (the woody perennial stem base, nearest PO term is stem base PO:0008039) absent. The aerial stems PO:0009047 are present (strigose or glabrous)
fix: 'caudex absent' denies only the persistent woody base. Because 'caudex' is a stem synonym in the PO lexicon, it must be mapped to stem base or held back. It must never become 'stem absent'.
reason: Eriogonum descriptions treat the caudex and the aerial flowering stems as different parts.

target: bract PO:0009055 absent only at the position just below the involucre. Leaflike bracts are present elsewhere on the inflorescence (e.g. at its nodes)
fix: '<part> absent immediately below/above/at <organ>' limits the absence to that position. Record it with the position, or not at all, and never as taxon-wide.
reason: A position phrase limits the absence. Bracts at other nodes are described.

target: stem kind: the aerial flowering stems (scapes) are absent. The caudex or vegetative stems are spreading
fix: '<modifier> stems absent' ('aerial flowering stems', 'wintering stems', 'trailing stems') denies only that kind of stem. Keep the modifier as the context, or drop the absence; never record 'stem absent'.
reason: In Eriogonum, the stems of the caudex and the aerial flowering stems are separate parts. The plant is acaulescent but has spreading caudex branches.

target: peduncle PO:0009053 present only in the fork of the proximal node, absent elsewhere. Where present it is slender
fix: '<part> absent except in/at <position>' means the part is present at that position. It is not an absence. Record presence at the position, or nothing.
reason: The 'except' clause states where the peduncles are found.

target: involucral bract PO:0009045 absent. 'thin' probably describes the floral scales (bract PO:0009055 subtending the flowers), which are present
fix: 'involucral bracts absent' must map to involucral bract PO:0009045, never to the general bract class. In Cyperaceae the floral scales are bracts that remain present.
reason: Eriophorum brachyantherum has a single spikelet with no involucral leaves, but its scales are described.

target: glandular trichome PO:0004509 (stalked gland) part of the leaf margin, absent PATO:0000462. The leaf lamina is present (base flat)
fix: '<part> without <feature>' ('margins without stalked glands') is the absence of the feature on that part. It is never the absence of the part or of the organ it belongs to.
reason: The statement denies the glands, not the lamina.

target: nectary PO:0009035 part of calyx (the calyx nectaries) absent. The leaf nectary on the abaxial midvein near the base is present
fix: In Malvaceae, a 'nectaries absent' statement in a calyx or flower description is about floral nectaries. The leaf (extrafloral) nectary is a different member. Scope the nectary by the organ named in the statement.
reason: FNA Hibiscus treats calyx nectaries and the leaf midvein nectary separately.

target: nectary PO:0009035 of the calyx absent. The leaf midvein nectary is only sometimes present
fix: Same as X00068: scope a nectary by its organ (calyx or leaf). 'sometimes present' is a variable trait and must never be recorded as plain 'present'.
reason: These are two different nectaries, and one of them is variable.

target: shoot axis/stem PO:0009047 not constricted (negation of constricted PATO:0001847), i.e. no annual growth constrictions. The whole plant is present
fix: In Huperzia/Lycopodiaceae, 'annual constrictions absent/present' says whether the shoot is constricted. It is a negated quality of the shoot, never the absence of the plant or the shoot.
reason: A constriction is a narrowing of the shoot, not a part. The PO-anchored misread defaulted to whole plant.

target: two different organs (e.g. the falls veined with purple or brown, and another organ such as the standards or spathes not veined). Both statements are about coloured veins, which is a colour pattern (multi-colored PATO:0001533 / streaked FLOPO:0991206) on the tepal PO:0009033, not vascular bundle presence
fix: In petaloid monocots, 'veined with <colour>' and 'not veined' describe a colour pattern on the organ named. Map them to a colour quality of that organ, never to 'vascular bundle present/absent'.
reason: Every perianth part has veins. These statements are about pigmentation, on different organs.

target: vascular bundle PO:0005020 of the organ described, not prominent (negation of prominent PATO:0001482). The sepals are veined with the colour of the limb (a colour pattern, not presence)
fix: 'not prominently <feature>' negates only prominence. The feature is present. It must never be read as an absence.
reason: 'Not prominently veined' implies the veins exist.

target: two different organs, e.g. the leaf apices not aristate and the phyllary apices apically aristate (or the other way round). The organ in each statement keeps it apart
fix: 'aristate' / 'not aristate' is an apex quality of the organ named in that statement. Scope it to that organ (its apex), never to a taxon-wide awn PO:0025349 present/absent.
reason: Isocoma descriptions give apex shapes for both leaves and phyllaries. Without the organ, the two read as contradictory.

target: cauline leaf PO:0000013 absent (the scape is leafless). The leaves are present and all basal
fix: 'leafless' in a stem or scape statement means the stem has no leaves (cauline leaves absent). It must never become 'leaf absent' for a plant whose leaves are described.
reason: Krigia dandelion has a basal rosette and leafless scapes.

target: bract PO:0009055 part of peduncle PO:0009053, absent PATO:0000462. The involucral bracts are present (linear-lanceolate)
fix: Same as X00060: 'Peduncles ebracteate' means the peduncle has no bracts. It never means the involucral bracts are absent.
reason: The phyllaries are described, so only the peduncle is without bracts.

target: the basal leaves (basal FLOPO:0991002) are absent. The cauline leaves PO:0000013 are present and sessile
fix: 'Basal/cauline leaves absent' denies only that member of the leaf series. Map it to cauline leaf PO:0000013, or keep the basal context. Never record it as 'leaf absent'.
reason: These are different members of the leaf series.

target: the cauline leaves PO:0000013 are absent. The basal leaves are present, ± sessile or tapered to a broad petiole
fix: Same as X00076: 'cauline leaves absent' must map to cauline leaf PO:0000013, never to vascular leaf.
reason: Lewisia has a basal rosette only, and that rosette is what is described.

target: the recurved flap (outgrowth) over the seed's hilum PO:0020063 is absent. No PO class exists for it, so drop the absence. The seed is present (surface ± smooth)
fix: '<modified noun> over/of/on <organ> absent' is the absence of the first noun, never of the organ after the preposition. If the first noun has no class, drop the absence.
reason: The seed is described. Only a seed-coat flap is denied.

target: staminode PO:0009077 (outer stamens without anthers, often petaloid). The fertile stamens have anthers. 'epidermis smooth' is probably the seed epidermis (seed PO:0009010 smooth), so the present statement is also misplaced
fix: '(outer) stamens/filaments without anthers' describes staminodes. Record staminode present, never 'anther absent' for the taxon.
reason: Mentzelia has staminodes and fertile stamens. 'Epidermis smooth' belongs to the seed description.

target: the petiole PO:0020038 is absent on the distal leaves. On the other (proximal) leaves the petiole is present or absent
fix: A parenthetical member ('absent (distal leaves)') limits the statement to that member. 'present or absent' is variable and must never be recorded as 'present'.
reason: Distal and proximal leaves differ, and the second statement is not an assertion of presence.

target: bract PO:0009055 present, not concealing the capsule (a negated relation/size quality, no class). Drop the absence; the bracts are green
fix: 'not <verb>ing <organ>' ('not concealing capsule') negates a relation of the subject. It is never the absence of the subject.
reason: The bracts exist and are described.

target: the petiole PO:0020038 is absent on the cauline leaves PO:0000013. On the basal leaves it is present or absent
fix: Same as X00076/X00080: the leading member ('Cauline leaves:', 'Basal leaves:') scopes everything after it. 'present or absent' is never presence.
reason: These are different members of the leaf series.

target: the petiole PO:0020038 is absent on one member (likely the distal/cauline leaves). It is present or absent on the other (basal/proximal) leaves
fix: Same as X00080/X00082: keep the leaf member. 'present or absent' is variable and must not be recorded as 'present'.
reason: This is the same Mentzelia pattern of basal and cauline leaves. The second statement is not a claim of presence.

target: either the petals PO:0009032 are usually absent but clawed when present (both_true, context 'rarely present'), or 'clawed' belongs to another organ (e.g. the sepals PO:0009031)
fix: 'petals absent' next to a petal description usually hides 'absent or rarely present'. Keep the frequency word. A statement with frequency 'rarely/sometimes' must not be tested as a taxon-wide absence.
reason: The epithet 'apetala' fits petals that are mostly absent. The short text does not show which organ is clawed.

target: axillary leaf clusters (short shoots or fascicles in the leaf axils) are absent. The main leaves PO:0009025 are present (flexuous)
fix: In Caryophyllaceae, 'axillary leaves absent' means there are no axillary leaf fascicles or short shoots. It never means the leaves are absent.
reason: The leaves are described. Only the secondary axillary clusters are denied.

target: stem kind: the overwintering stems are absent. The flowering stems PO:0009047 are erect
fix: Same as X00064: '<modifier> stems absent' ('wintering', 'trailing', 'sterile', 'aerial') denies only that kind of stem.
reason: These are different kinds of stem.

target: stem kind: the trailing stems are absent. The stems PO:0009047 are ascending
fix: Same as X00064/X00086.
reason: These are different kinds of stem.

target: bract PO:0009055 part of peduncle/scape PO:0009053, absent. The involucral bracts PO:0009045 are present, with acuminate apices
fix: Same as X00060: 'Stems (peduncles) ebracteate' means the stalk has no bracts, never that the involucral bracts are absent.
reason: The phyllaries are described.

target: the tubercles PO:0025352 and spines are absent on one member (likely the fruit or upper areoles). The stem spines are present. Cactus spines are spine leaf PO:0025173, not thorn PO:0025172
fix: In Cactaceae, 'tubercles and spines absent' in a fruit or flower-tube statement is about that organ only. Scope it to that organ, and map cactus 'spines' to spine leaf PO:0025173, never thorn.
reason: Lophocereus schottii has spiny stems. The absence is about another member (probably the fruit).
